place.source_title: Anderson Carriage Manufacturing Company, Twenty-fifth & Walton Streets

brief: Plain three-storey red-brick factory of about 1900 on a corner, with regular segmental-arched windows, a flat roof behind a low parapet, two large vehicle doors at street level and a long two-storey wing running back along the side street. Built for a carriage maker that tried and failed to switch to motor cars; now a body shop and storage.

facade.notes: the Anderson Carriage Manufacturing Co. (Anderson IN, c.1900), HAER: a plain red-brick factory on a corner, a stepped parapet, segmental-arched windows partly bricked in, two big overhead vehicle doors; a later three-storey section in back; utility poles and a nearly empty street

why.note: before electric motors and steel frames, a factory was a narrow tall masonry block: daylight from both sides, power from one line shaft or a waterwheel
